source: USDA FoodData Central, SR Legacy (April 2018 release), https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/ - public domain. Nutrients are per the listed household serving, scaled from the USDA per-100 g values. Entries with a negative fdc_id are not USDA records; their values come from product labels.

foods.name: Grapes, red or green, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Low potassium at 1/2 cup (about 15 grapes); a full bowl is 300+ mg.

foods.name: Peach, raw
foods.kidney_notes: A fresh peach has about twice the potassium of canned peaches in juice; keep to one small one.

foods.name: Pear, raw
foods.kidney_notes: One small pear stays under 200 mg potassium; a medium one is about 206 mg.

foods.name: Watermelon, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Low potassium per cup, but it is mostly water: count it toward fluid if you have a fluid limit and stop at 1 cup.

foods.name: Tangerine (mandarin), raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium; one small tangerine is the usual citrus swap for an orange.

foods.name: Grapefruit, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium; grapefruit also interacts with several medicines (statins, some transplant and blood-pressure drugs), so ask your pharmacist.

foods.name: Orange, raw
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~240 mg); a tangerine, or a cup of berries or grapes, is the renal-diet swap.

foods.name: Banana, raw
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~420 mg); a renal dietitian usually suggests apples, berries or grapes instead.

foods.name: Cantaloupe, raw
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~430 mg per cup); watermelon or pineapple is the lower-potassium melon choice.

foods.name: Honeydew melon, raw
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~390 mg per cup); swap for watermelon or pineapple.

foods.name: Kiwifruit, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~215 mg); one small kiwi is fine occasionally, berries are the safer everyday pick.

foods.name: Mango, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium and 23 g sugar per cup; stick to 1/2 cup or swap for pineapple.

foods.name: Papaya, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~260 mg per cup); pineapple or canned peaches are lower.

foods.name: Nectarine, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~285 mg); a plum or canned peaches in juice are lower.

foods.name: Apricots, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium fresh, and very high once dried; keep to two fresh ones.

foods.name: Figs, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~230 mg); dried figs are far worse, so keep to fresh and small.

foods.name: Pomegranate arils
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~205 mg per 1/2 cup); berries are the lower-potassium swap.

foods.name: Avocado, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~240 mg in just a quarter); use a thin smear or swap for cream cheese or hummus.

foods.name: Apricots, dried
foods.kidney_notes: Dried fruit concentrates potassium (~400 mg in 10 halves); have fresh fruit or a few grapes instead.

foods.name: Raisins
foods.kidney_notes: Dried fruit concentrates potassium (~320 mg per small box) and sugar; fresh grapes are the swap.

foods.name: Prunes (dried plums)
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~350 mg) and phosphorus; if you need them for constipation, ask your dietitian about an alternative.

foods.name: Dates, medjool
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~330 mg for two) and sugar; a few grapes or a small hard candy are the swaps.

foods.name: Plantain, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~370 mg per 1/2 cup); white rice or pasta are the lower-potassium starch swaps.

foods.name: Star fruit (carambola)
foods.kidney_notes: AVOID with kidney disease: star fruit contains a neurotoxin (caramboxin) that failing kidneys cannot clear; it can cause hiccups, confusion, seizures and death.

foods.name: Broccoli, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~230 mg per 1/2 cup); cauliflower, cabbage or green beans are lower.

foods.name: Broccoli, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~290 mg per cup raw); boiling and draining removes some.

foods.name: Zucchini, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~235 mg per 1/2 cup); summer squash is similar, so keep portions small.

foods.name: Corn, sweet, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~220 mg) and about 20 g carbs per ear; count it as a starch.

foods.name: Mushrooms, white, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~220 mg per cup) and phosphorus; keep to 1/2 cup.

foods.name: Peas, green, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~220 mg) and phosphorus per 1/2 cup; green beans are the lower swap.

foods.name: Potato, boiled, peeled
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium even peeled (~255 mg per 1/2 cup); leach it: peel, dice small, soak in a large pot of water 2-4 h, then boil in fresh water, and keep to 1/2 cup.

foods.name: Potato, baked, with skin
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~925 mg); the skin is worst. Swap for white rice, pasta, or a small portion of leached boiled potato.

foods.name: Mashed potatoes, with milk
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~300 mg per 1/2 cup) plus milk phosphorus; make it with leached potatoes and rice milk or swap for rice.

foods.name: French fries, frozen, oven-heated
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~360 mg) and salted; a small portion of white rice or pasta is the swap.

foods.name: Sweet potato, baked
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~475 mg per 1/2 cup); white rice, pasta or leached white potato are lower.

foods.name: Tomato, raw
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~290 mg); a few cherry tomatoes or roasted red pepper give colour with less potassium.

foods.name: Tomato sauce, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~400 mg per 1/2 cup) and sodium; use a little tomato paste thinned with water, or a garlic-and-oil sauce.

foods.name: Tomato paste, no salt added
foods.kidney_notes: Concentrated potassium (~160 mg per tbsp); a tablespoon for flavour is fine, a cup is not.

foods.name: Spinach, raw
foods.kidney_notes: Fine raw in a salad (~165 mg potassium per cup); cooked spinach packs 5x more into the same space.

foods.name: Spinach, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~420 mg per 1/2 cup); swap for cabbage, green beans or a raw spinach salad.

foods.name: Kale, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~170 mg per cup); cabbage is the lower leafy swap.

foods.name: Brussels sprouts, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~245 mg per 1/2 cup); cauliflower or cabbage are lower.

foods.name: Beets, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~260 mg per 1/2 cup); carrots or radishes are lower.

foods.name: Butternut squash, baked
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~290 mg per 1/2 cup); summer squash or carrots are lower.

foods.name: Pumpkin, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~250 mg per 1/2 cup); keep to a small portion.

foods.name: Artichoke, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~345 mg per artichoke); asparagus or green beans are lower.

foods.name: Pickle, dill
foods.kidney_notes: Very high sodium (~280 mg per small spear, ~1100 mg for a large pickle); cucumber slices with vinegar and dill are the swap.

foods.name: Sauerkraut, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Very high sodium (~470 mg per 1/2 cup); rinse well or swap for boiled cabbage with vinegar.

foods.name: Olives, ripe, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Brined, so high sodium (~320 mg for 10); a few are fine, a handful is not.

foods.name: Bread, whole-wheat
foods.kidney_notes: Whole grains carry more phosphorus and potassium than white; white or sourdough bread is the usual renal swap (talk to your dietitian about fibre).

foods.name: Bread, multigrain
foods.kidney_notes: Seeds and whole grains add phosphorus and potassium; white or light rye bread is lower.

foods.name: Bagel, plain
foods.kidney_notes: One bagel is about 50 g carbs (3+ carb choices) and ~420 mg sodium; half a bagel is a more realistic portion.

foods.name: Tortilla, flour
foods.kidney_notes: Most store-bought flour tortillas use phosphate leavening (sodium acid pyrophosphate); corn tortillas are the lower-phosphorus choice.

foods.name: Cornbread, from recipe
foods.kidney_notes: Baking powder, milk and cornmeal make this moderately high in phosphorus; keep to one small piece.

foods.name: Muffin, blueberry, commercial
foods.kidney_notes: Commercial muffins use phosphate leavening and are ~55 g carbs; a slice of white toast with jam is the swap.

foods.name: Pancakes, from recipe
foods.kidney_notes: Baking powder and milk add phosphorus (~120 mg for two); use a low-sodium, phosphate-free baking powder and rice milk.

foods.name: Pancakes, from complete mix
foods.kidney_notes: Pancake mixes rely on phosphate leavening (highly absorbed phosphorus) and are salty; homemade with rice milk is the swap.

foods.name: Waffles, frozen
foods.kidney_notes: Frozen waffles list sodium/calcium phosphates for leavening; homemade or a slice of white toast is lower in phosphorus.

foods.name: Biscuit, refrigerated dough, baked
foods.kidney_notes: Canned biscuit dough is leavened with sodium acid pyrophosphate and is salty (~510 mg sodium); a white roll is the swap.

foods.name: Rice, brown, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Brown rice has about 3x the phosphorus and twice the potassium of white rice; white rice is the renal-diet grain.

foods.name: Pasta, whole-wheat, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Whole-wheat pasta roughly doubles the phosphorus of regular pasta; regular pasta is the swap.

foods.name: Quinoa, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: High in both potassium (~320 mg) and phosphorus (~280 mg) per cup; white rice or couscous is the swap.

foods.name: Oatmeal, cooked (regular or quick oats)
foods.kidney_notes: Oats are moderately high in phosphorus (~180 mg per cup); cream of wheat, grits or cream of rice are the lower-phosphorus hot cereals.

foods.name: Oatmeal, instant, fortified, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: Flavoured instant oats are fortified and salted; check the label for added phosphates, or choose cream of wheat.

foods.name: Toasted oat cereal (Cheerios-type)
foods.kidney_notes: Oat cereals carry more phosphorus than corn or rice cereals; fine occasionally.

foods.name: Shredded wheat cereal
foods.kidney_notes: Whole-wheat cereal is high in phosphorus (~190 mg per cup); corn flakes or crisp rice are the low-phosphorus swaps.

foods.name: Raisin bran cereal
foods.kidney_notes: Bran plus raisins: very high potassium (~360 mg) and phosphorus (~230 mg) per cup; swap for corn flakes or crisp rice.

foods.name: Bran cereal (shredded wheat and bran)
foods.kidney_notes: Bran cereals are among the highest-phosphorus breakfast foods (~250 mg per serving); corn flakes, crisp rice or cream of wheat are the swaps.

foods.name: Snack crackers (buttery round)
foods.kidney_notes: Buttery snack crackers usually list calcium phosphate leavening and salt; unsalted saltines or rice cakes are lower.

foods.name: Crackers, whole-wheat
foods.kidney_notes: Whole-grain crackers are higher in phosphorus and potassium; saltines or rice cakes are the swap.

foods.name: Milk, whole
foods.kidney_notes: A cup of milk is ~320 mg potassium and ~205 mg phosphorus; many renal plans allow 1/2 cup a day or swap to rice milk.

foods.name: Milk, 2% reduced fat
foods.kidney_notes: A cup of milk is ~340 mg potassium and ~225 mg phosphorus; keep to 1/2 cup or swap to unenriched rice milk.

foods.name: Milk, skim (nonfat)
foods.kidney_notes: Skim milk has slightly more potassium and phosphorus per cup than whole; the fat is not the renal issue, the minerals are.

foods.name: Chocolate milk, 2%
foods.kidney_notes: Milk minerals plus cocoa: ~420 mg potassium and ~250 mg phosphorus, and 24 g sugar; rice milk with a little vanilla is the swap.

foods.name: Buttermilk, low fat
foods.kidney_notes: Same potassium and phosphorus load as milk, with extra sodium.

foods.name: Yogurt, plain, low fat
foods.kidney_notes: Yogurt is concentrated milk: ~390 mg potassium and ~240 mg phosphorus per 6 oz; a 4 oz portion or a non-dairy yogurt is the swap.

foods.name: Greek yogurt, plain, nonfat
foods.kidney_notes: Straining removes some potassium and phosphorus, but 6 oz is still ~17 g protein and ~230 mg phosphorus; count it as a protein portion.

foods.name: Yogurt, fruit, low fat
foods.kidney_notes: Milk minerals plus ~30 g sugar; a small plain yogurt with fresh berries is the swap.

foods.name: Cheese, cheddar
foods.kidney_notes: Hard cheeses are high in phosphorus (~130 mg per oz) and salt; 1 oz a day is a common limit, cream cheese is lower.

foods.name: Cheese, mozzarella, part skim
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate phosphorus (~130 mg per oz); fine in a 1 oz portion.

foods.name: Cheese, Swiss
foods.kidney_notes: Lower in sodium than most cheeses but higher in phosphorus (~160 mg per oz); keep to one slice.

foods.name: Cottage cheese, 2%
foods.kidney_notes: High sodium (~350 mg per 1/2 cup) and phosphorus; ricotta or a no-salt-added cottage cheese is the swap.

foods.name: Ricotta cheese, part skim
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate phosphorus (~225 mg per 1/2 cup); keep the portion small.

foods.name: Cheese, American, processed
foods.kidney_notes: Processed cheese is made with sodium phosphate emulsifiers (almost fully absorbed) and is very salty; natural Swiss or cream cheese is the swap.

foods.name: Parmesan cheese, grated
foods.kidney_notes: Very concentrated in sodium and phosphorus per gram; a tablespoon sprinkle is fine, a pile is not.

foods.name: Feta cheese
foods.kidney_notes: Brined, so high sodium (~320 mg per oz); a small crumble goes a long way.

foods.name: Non-dairy creamer, liquid
foods.kidney_notes: Most non-dairy creamers contain dipotassium phosphate; a splash of real half and half is the lower-phosphorus choice.

foods.name: Rice milk, unsweetened
foods.kidney_notes: The classic renal milk swap: low potassium and phosphorus (check the label for added phosphate 'enrichment').

foods.name: Almond milk, unsweetened
foods.kidney_notes: Low potassium and phosphorus naturally, but many brands add calcium or potassium phosphate; read the ingredient list.

foods.name: Soy milk, unsweetened
foods.kidney_notes: Higher in potassium and phosphorus than rice or almond milk, and often fortified with phosphate; rice milk is the lower swap.

foods.name: Chicken breast, batter-fried
foods.kidney_notes: Batter adds sodium and phosphate leavening; roasted or grilled chicken is the swap.

foods.name: Bacon, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Cured with salt and usually sodium phosphate; two slices is the limit, or choose an uncured, no-phosphate brand.

foods.name: Ham, extra lean, roasted
foods.kidney_notes: Cured ham is ~1000 mg sodium per 3 oz and is typically injected with sodium phosphate; fresh roasted pork is the swap.

foods.name: Deli ham, sliced
foods.kidney_notes: Deli meats are salty and phosphate-injected; slice your own roasted chicken, turkey or pork instead.

foods.name: Deli turkey breast, sliced
foods.kidney_notes: Even 'lean' deli turkey is brined with salt and sodium phosphate; home-roasted turkey breast is the swap.

foods.name: Pork sausage, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Sausage is high in sodium and often phosphate-cured; fresh ground pork or turkey seasoned at home is the swap.

foods.name: Hot dog, beef
foods.kidney_notes: Hot dogs combine ~410 mg sodium with sodium phosphate; a grilled chicken thigh or a fresh pork patty is the swap.

foods.name: Bologna, beef and pork
foods.kidney_notes: Processed luncheon meat: salt, sodium phosphate and nitrite; roast your own meat for sandwiches.

foods.name: Salami, dry
foods.kidney_notes: Very high sodium (~500 mg in three slices); a slice of fresh roast beef is the swap.

foods.name: Pepperoni
foods.kidney_notes: Very salty cured meat (~450 mg sodium per oz); use a few slices for flavour, not a layer.

foods.name: Corned beef, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Brine-cured: ~830 mg sodium per 3 oz; fresh brisket or pot roast is the swap.

foods.name: Beef jerky
foods.kidney_notes: Very high sodium (~500 mg per oz) and concentrated phosphorus; unsalted popcorn or a hard-boiled egg white is the snack swap.

foods.name: Beef liver, braised
foods.kidney_notes: Organ meats are extremely high in phosphorus (~420 mg per 3 oz); choose lean muscle meat instead.

foods.name: Egg, hard-boiled
foods.kidney_notes: The yolk holds the phosphorus (~85 mg per egg); egg whites are the renal favourite and still give the protein.

foods.name: Salmon, Atlantic, farmed, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Excellent protein but ~325 mg potassium and ~215 mg phosphorus per 3 oz; a 3 oz portion is the point to stop.

foods.name: Salmon, sockeye, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Wild salmon runs ~300+ mg potassium per 3 oz; keep to one portion.

foods.name: Salmon, pink, canned, drained
foods.kidney_notes: Canned fish is salted (~350 mg sodium); rinse, and choose boneless so the bones do not add phosphorus.

foods.name: Tuna, light, canned in water, drained
foods.kidney_notes: A good lower-phosphorus fish, but canned in brine (~210 mg sodium); look for 'no salt added'.

foods.name: Tuna, white (albacore), canned in water
foods.kidney_notes: Canned in brine (~300 mg sodium); choose 'no salt added' and drain well.

foods.name: Tuna, yellowfin, fresh, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Fresh tuna is one of the higher-potassium fish (~480 mg per 3 oz); cod, tilapia or haddock are lower.

foods.name: Halibut, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~450 mg per 3 oz); cod, haddock or tilapia are the lower white-fish choices.

foods.name: Mackerel, Atlantic, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Oily fish rich in omega-3 but ~340 mg potassium and ~235 mg phosphorus per 3 oz; keep to one portion.

foods.name: Sardines, canned in oil, with bones
foods.kidney_notes: The edible bones make sardines one of the highest-phosphorus foods (~450 mg per can) and they are salty; canned tuna is the swap.

foods.name: Smoked salmon (lox)
foods.kidney_notes: Smoked and salted: ~1100 mg sodium per 2 oz; fresh baked salmon is the swap.

foods.name: Shrimp, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Most frozen shrimp are soaked in sodium tripolyphosphate brine (the USDA entry notes 'additives to retain moisture'); look for 'no additives' or 'dry' shrimp.

foods.name: Lobster, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Naturally high in sodium (~410 mg per 3 oz); skip the salted butter.

foods.name: Clams, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Very high sodium (~1000 mg) and phosphorus (~290 mg) per 3 oz; keep to a small portion.

foods.name: Fish sticks, frozen, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: Breaded fish sticks are salty and usually treated with sodium tripolyphosphate; bake a plain white fish fillet instead.

foods.name: Imitation crab (surimi)
foods.kidney_notes: Surimi is processed with salt, sugar and phosphates; real crab or cooked white fish is the swap.

foods.name: Black beans, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Beans give ~300 mg potassium and ~120 mg phosphorus per 1/2 cup; a 1/2 cup counts as both a protein and a starch, and canned beans rinsed well lose some potassium.

foods.name: Kidney beans, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~360 mg per 1/2 cup) and phosphorus; rinse canned beans and keep to 1/2 cup.

foods.name: Pinto beans, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~375 mg per 1/2 cup) and phosphorus; rinse canned beans and keep to 1/2 cup.

foods.name: Navy beans, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~355 mg per 1/2 cup) and phosphorus; keep portions small.

foods.name: Chickpeas (garbanzo), cooked
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate-high potassium (~240 mg) and phosphorus (~140 mg) per 1/2 cup; hummus in a 2 tbsp portion is the gentler way to eat them.

foods.name: Lentils, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~365 mg per 1/2 cup) and phosphorus; keep to 1/2 cup and count it as your protein.

foods.name: Split peas, cooked
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~355 mg per 1/2 cup) and phosphorus; keep to 1/2 cup.

foods.name: Lima beans, boiled
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~485 mg per 1/2 cup); green beans are the swap.

foods.name: Baked beans, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Canned baked beans add ~430 mg sodium and sugar to the bean potassium; plain beans you season yourself are the swap.

foods.name: Refried beans, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Canned refried beans are salty (~450 mg per 1/2 cup) on top of the bean potassium; keep to 1/4 cup.

foods.name: Tofu, firm
foods.kidney_notes: A kidney-friendly protein: 1/4 block is ~7 g protein with ~100 mg phosphorus (plant phosphorus is poorly absorbed); calcium-set brands add calcium.

foods.name: Edamame, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~340 mg per 1/2 cup) and phosphorus; green beans are the snack swap.

foods.name: Soy nuts (roasted soybeans)
foods.kidney_notes: Extremely concentrated potassium (~600 mg) and phosphorus (~150 mg) per 1/4 cup; unsalted popcorn is the crunchy swap.

foods.name: Peanut butter
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~180 mg) and phosphorus (~110 mg) per 2 tbsp; 1 tbsp is a sensible portion, cream cheese or jam are swaps.

foods.name: Peanuts, dry roasted, salted
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~180 mg) and phosphorus (~100 mg) per oz plus salt; a small handful of unsalted is the limit.

foods.name: Almonds
foods.kidney_notes: Nuts are concentrated phosphorus (~135 mg per oz) and potassium (~210 mg); macadamias or pecans are the lower-mineral nuts.

foods.name: Walnuts
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~120 mg) and phosphorus (~100 mg) per oz; keep to a small handful.

foods.name: Cashews, dry roasted, salted
foods.kidney_notes: High phosphorus (~140 mg) and potassium (~160 mg) per oz plus salt; macadamias are the lower swap.

foods.name: Pistachios, dry roasted, salted
foods.kidney_notes: High potassium (~290 mg per oz) and phosphorus; pecans or macadamias are lower.

foods.name: Pecans
foods.kidney_notes: One of the lower-potassium nuts (~115 mg per oz); still a phosphorus source, so keep to 1 oz.

foods.name: Macadamia nuts
foods.kidney_notes: The lowest-potassium, lowest-phosphorus common nut; the usual renal-diet nut choice in a 1 oz portion.

foods.name: Mixed nuts, dry roasted, salted
foods.kidney_notes: Salted mixed nuts bring ~170 mg potassium, ~130 mg phosphorus and salt per oz; unsalted macadamias are the swap.

foods.name: Sunflower seeds, dry roasted, salted
foods.kidney_notes: Among the highest-phosphorus snacks (~325 mg per oz) and salted; unsalted popcorn is the swap.

foods.name: Pumpkin seeds, roasted, salted
foods.kidney_notes: Very high phosphorus (~350 mg) and potassium (~230 mg) per oz; unsalted popcorn or a few macadamias instead.

foods.name: Chia seeds
foods.kidney_notes: Concentrated phosphorus (~100 mg per tbsp); a teaspoon stirred in is plenty.

foods.name: Coffee, brewed
foods.kidney_notes: Black coffee is ~115 mg potassium per cup; a cup or two is fine, and it counts toward any fluid limit.

foods.name: Cola, regular
foods.kidney_notes: Dark colas get their tang from phosphoric acid (fully absorbed phosphorus) and carry ~39 g sugar; a clear soda, or sparkling water with lemon, is the swap.

foods.name: Cola, diet
foods.kidney_notes: Sugar-free, but still phosphoric acid (~35 mg phosphorus per can, essentially all of it absorbed); diet lemon-lime or sparkling water is the swap.

foods.name: Pepper-type soda, regular
foods.kidney_notes: Contains phosphoric acid and ~40 g sugar; clear soda or sparkling water is the swap.

foods.name: Lemon-lime soda, regular
foods.kidney_notes: No phosphoric acid, so a clear soda is the renal choice for treating a low: 4 fl oz is about 13 g carbs. A whole 12 oz can is 3 servings and 38 g of sugar.

foods.name: Ginger ale
foods.kidney_notes: Clear and phosphate-free: 4 fl oz (about 11 g carbs) treats a low. A whole 12 oz can is 3 servings and 32 g of sugar.

foods.name: Root beer
foods.kidney_notes: Usually no phosphoric acid, but ~40 g sugar per can; diet or sparkling water otherwise.

foods.name: Club soda
foods.kidney_notes: Fine, but check the label: club soda has added sodium (~75 mg per can), plain seltzer has none.

foods.name: Apple juice
foods.kidney_notes: 4 fl oz is ~14 g fast carbs and only ~125 mg potassium, which is why apple juice is the usual hypo drink for CKD; a full glass doubles everything.

foods.name: Grape juice
foods.kidney_notes: 4 fl oz is ~19 g fast carbs with low potassium, so it works for treating a low; not an everyday drink.

foods.name: Cranberry juice cocktail
foods.kidney_notes: The lowest-potassium juice (~18 mg per 1/2 cup) and NIDDK's named alternative to orange juice for treating a low (4 fl oz is ~17 g fast carbs); the light version is the everyday choice.

foods.name: Orange juice
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~495 mg per cup) and 21 g sugar; apple, grape or cranberry juice are the low-potassium swaps.

foods.name: Pineapple juice
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium (~160 mg per 4 fl oz); apple or cranberry juice are lower.

foods.name: Prune juice
foods.kidney_notes: Extremely high potassium (~700 mg per cup); if you need help with constipation ask your care team about a laxative instead.

foods.name: Tomato juice
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~560 mg) and sodium (~650 mg) per cup; cranberry or apple juice are the swaps.

foods.name: Vegetable juice cocktail (V8-type)
foods.kidney_notes: Very high potassium (~470 mg) and sodium (~480 mg) per cup; eat low-potassium vegetables instead of drinking them.

foods.name: Lemonade, from powder
foods.kidney_notes: Low potassium; sugar varies widely by brand (this USDA entry is ~9 g per cup, many bottled lemonades are 25+ g), so check the label or choose sugar-free.

foods.name: Fruit punch drink
foods.kidney_notes: Low in minerals but ~30 g sugar per cup; a sugar-free drink is the swap.

foods.name: Sports drink (lemon-lime)
foods.kidney_notes: Low potassium, so 8 fl oz (~19 g carbs) can treat a low; otherwise it is sugar water with ~110 mg sodium per cup.

foods.name: Energy drink
foods.kidney_notes: ~27 g sugar plus caffeine and taurine; not recommended with kidney disease, and sugar-free versions still add caffeine.

foods.name: Coconut water
foods.kidney_notes: Marketed as healthy but ~400 mg potassium per cup; water or a low-potassium juice is the swap.

foods.name: Nutritional shake (Boost Plus-type)
foods.kidney_notes: Standard nutrition shakes are high in potassium and phosphorus; renal formulas (e.g. Nepro, Novasource Renal) are made for CKD, ask your dietitian.

foods.name: Hot cocoa, from mix with water
foods.kidney_notes: Cocoa brings potassium and phosphorus and the mix adds sugar; keep it occasional.

foods.name: Milkshake, chocolate, thick
foods.kidney_notes: Milk plus chocolate: ~670 mg potassium, ~380 mg phosphorus and ~60 g sugar; a small sherbet is the treat swap.

foods.name: Beer, regular
foods.kidney_notes: Moderate potassium and phosphorus (~95 and ~50 mg per can) and it counts as fluid; alcohol also raises hypo risk with insulin.

foods.name: Beer, light
foods.kidney_notes: Lower carbs than regular beer but the same fluid and hypo caution with insulin.

foods.name: Wine, red
foods.kidney_notes: ~190 mg potassium per glass; one glass is usually fine, and it counts toward fluid.

foods.name: Wine, white
foods.kidney_notes: Lower potassium than red (~105 mg per glass); counts toward fluid, and alcohol raises hypo risk.

foods.name: Spirits (gin, rum, vodka, whiskey), 80 proof
foods.kidney_notes: No potassium or phosphorus, but alcohol on insulin can cause delayed lows; mix with diet or clear soda, not cola.

foods.name: Hard candy
foods.kidney_notes: Pure sugar with no potassium or phosphorus: 3 pieces (~17 g carbs) is a renal-safe way to treat a low.

foods.name: Jelly beans
foods.kidney_notes: About 15 g fast carbs with no minerals; a renal-safe hypo treatment.

foods.name: Marshmallows
foods.kidney_notes: Low in potassium and phosphorus; a renal-diet friendly sweet, but ~24 g fast carbs.

foods.name: Milk chocolate bar
foods.kidney_notes: Chocolate is high in potassium (~165 mg) and phosphorus (~90 mg) per bar; hard candy, marshmallows or a vanilla wafer are the swaps.

foods.name: Dark chocolate, 70-85% cacao
foods.kidney_notes: The darker the chocolate the more potassium (~200 mg per oz) and phosphorus; a small square is the limit.

foods.name: Peanut butter cups
foods.kidney_notes: Chocolate plus peanuts: ~155 mg potassium and ~70 mg phosphorus; hard candy or a vanilla cookie is the swap.

foods.name: Cookies, chocolate chip
foods.kidney_notes: Chocolate chips add potassium and phosphorus; sugar cookies, shortbread or vanilla wafers are the lower-mineral cookies.

foods.name: Cookies, chocolate sandwich (Oreo-type)
foods.kidney_notes: Cocoa plus phosphate leavening in many brands; a vanilla sandwich cookie or shortbread is the swap.

foods.name: Cake, yellow, with vanilla frosting
foods.kidney_notes: Commercial cake uses phosphate leavening and is ~38 g carbs a slice; angel food cake is the lower-phosphorus treat.

foods.name: Cake, chocolate, with chocolate frosting
foods.kidney_notes: Chocolate cake stacks cocoa potassium on phosphate leavening; angel food or a plain yellow cake is the swap.

foods.name: Cake, angel food
foods.kidney_notes: Egg-white cake with almost no fat, potassium or phosphorus: a favourite renal-diet dessert (still ~16 g carbs).

foods.name: Cheesecake
foods.kidney_notes: Cream cheese keeps potassium modest but it is ~75 mg phosphorus and ~350 mg sodium a slice and very rich; a small slice occasionally.

foods.name: Pie, apple
foods.kidney_notes: Apple pie is one of the lower-potassium pies but ~40 g carbs a slice; skip pumpkin, pecan and chocolate pies.

foods.name: Doughnut, glazed
foods.kidney_notes: Yeast doughnuts still use phosphate leavening and are fried; a plain cake slice or a sugar cookie is the swap.

foods.name: Brownie
foods.kidney_notes: Chocolate and often phosphate leavening; a blondie without chocolate chips or angel food cake is the swap.

foods.name: Toaster pastry, frosted
foods.kidney_notes: Frosted toaster pastries list sodium acid pyrophosphate and are 37 g carbs each; white toast with jam is the swap.

foods.name: Ice cream, vanilla
foods.kidney_notes: Dairy, so ~70 mg phosphorus and ~130 mg potassium per 1/2 cup; it melts to liquid, so it counts toward fluid.

foods.name: Ice cream, chocolate
foods.kidney_notes: Chocolate ice cream has about half again the potassium of vanilla; sherbet or vanilla is the swap, and it counts as fluid.

foods.name: Sherbet, orange
foods.kidney_notes: Lower in phosphorus and potassium than ice cream, so the usual frozen-dessert swap; counts toward fluid.

foods.name: Frozen yogurt, vanilla, soft-serve
foods.kidney_notes: Dairy minerals similar to ice cream; counts toward fluid.

foods.name: Popsicle (ice pop)
foods.kidney_notes: No minerals, but it is frozen sugar water: count it toward fluid and as ~11 g fast carbs.

foods.name: Popsicle, sugar-free
foods.kidney_notes: A good way to soothe thirst on a fluid limit, but it still counts as ~50 mL of fluid.

foods.name: Gelatin dessert (Jell-O)
foods.kidney_notes: Low potassium and phosphorus, but it is a liquid at body temperature so it counts toward fluid, and ~19 g fast carbs.

foods.name: Gelatin dessert, sugar-free
foods.kidney_notes: A classic renal-diet snack with almost nothing in it; still counts toward a fluid limit.

foods.name: Pudding, vanilla, ready-to-eat
foods.kidney_notes: Shelf-stable pudding cups thicken with sodium/tetrasodium phosphate on top of milk phosphorus; sugar-free gelatin is the swap.

foods.name: Pudding, chocolate, ready-to-eat
foods.kidney_notes: Chocolate pudding cups add cocoa potassium to phosphate additives; sugar-free gelatin or a sherbet is the swap.

foods.name: Honey
foods.kidney_notes: About 17 g fast carbs with negligible potassium: usable to treat a low.

foods.name: Sugar, granulated
foods.kidney_notes: A tablespoon is ~13 g pure glucose/fructose with no minerals: a hypo treatment in a pinch.

foods.name: Maple syrup
foods.kidney_notes: Low in minerals but ~13 g sugar per tbsp; sugar-free syrup is the everyday swap.

foods.name: Potato chips, salted
foods.kidney_notes: Potato chips are high in potassium (~350 mg per oz) and salt; unsalted popcorn, pretzels or rice cakes are the swaps.

foods.name: Tortilla chips, salted
foods.kidney_notes: Lower potassium than potato chips but ~90 mg sodium per oz; unsalted popcorn is the swap.

foods.name: Cheese puffs
foods.kidney_notes: Cheese-powder snacks are salty and contain phosphate emulsifiers; unsalted popcorn is the swap.

foods.name: Pork rinds
foods.kidney_notes: Very high sodium (~520 mg per oz); unsalted popcorn is the crunchy swap.

foods.name: Popcorn, air-popped, unsalted
foods.kidney_notes: The renal-diet snack: low potassium, phosphorus and sodium when unsalted.

foods.name: Popcorn, microwave, regular
foods.kidney_notes: Microwave bags add ~300 mg sodium and butter flavouring; air-popped is the swap.

foods.name: Pretzels, hard, salted
foods.kidney_notes: Low potassium and phosphorus but ~350 mg sodium per oz; unsalted pretzels or rice cakes are the swap.

foods.name: Granola bar, hard, plain
foods.kidney_notes: Oats and nuts make granola bars moderately high in phosphorus; a rice-cereal bar or vanilla wafers are lower.

foods.name: Trail mix
foods.kidney_notes: Nuts plus dried fruit: ~260 mg potassium and ~130 mg phosphorus per 1/4 cup; unsalted popcorn or a few macadamias is the swap.

foods.name: Fruit snacks (fruit leather)
foods.kidney_notes: Mostly sugar with little potassium: fast carbs that can treat a low, but not a fruit serving.

foods.name: Salt, table
foods.kidney_notes: A quarter teaspoon is ~580 mg sodium, over a quarter of a 2000 mg day; season with herbs, pepper, lemon, vinegar and garlic instead.

foods.name: Salt substitute (potassium chloride, e.g. NoSalt, Nu-Salt)
foods.kidney_notes: AVOID with kidney disease: salt substitutes are potassium chloride, ~610 mg potassium per 1/4 tsp, and can push blood potassium to dangerous levels; use herbs, lemon or salt-free herb blends (check they are KCl-free).

foods.name: Lite salt (half sodium, half potassium chloride)
foods.kidney_notes: AVOID with kidney disease: 'lite' salt is half potassium chloride (~350 mg potassium per 1/4 tsp) and still a quarter of the day's sodium; use herbs and spices.

foods.name: Baking powder (phosphate type)
foods.kidney_notes: Standard baking powder is sodium acid pyrophosphate or monocalcium phosphate: ~455 mg phosphorus (almost fully absorbed) and ~365 mg sodium per tsp, roughly 40-75 mg phosphorus per slice of a 12-serving cake; use a low-sodium, phosphate-free baking powder.

foods.name: Soy sauce
foods.kidney_notes: ~880 mg sodium in one tablespoon (almost half a day's limit); use a teaspoon, dilute with water, or try lemon and ginger.

foods.name: Soy sauce, reduced sodium
foods.kidney_notes: 'Reduced' still means ~530 mg sodium per tablespoon; measure with a teaspoon.

foods.name: Teriyaki sauce
foods.kidney_notes: ~690 mg sodium per tablespoon plus sugar; make your own with a little reduced-sodium soy, garlic, ginger and pineapple juice.

foods.name: Worcestershire sauce
foods.kidney_notes: Moderately salty (~220 mg sodium per tbsp) and made with anchovies and molasses (potassium); a splash is fine.

foods.name: Ketchup
foods.kidney_notes: ~150 mg sodium and 4 g sugar per tbsp, plus tomato potassium; a tablespoon is fine, or use a low-sodium ketchup.

foods.name: Ranch dressing
foods.kidney_notes: ~260 mg sodium per 2 tbsp and many brands add disodium phosphate; oil and vinegar or lemon is the swap.

foods.name: Italian dressing
foods.kidney_notes: Bottled Italian is ~290 mg sodium per 2 tbsp; mix your own with olive oil, vinegar, garlic and herbs.

foods.name: Caesar dressing
foods.kidney_notes: Parmesan and anchovy make Caesar dressing salty (~360 mg per 2 tbsp); use half the amount or an oil-and-lemon dressing.

foods.name: Barbecue sauce
foods.kidney_notes: ~350 mg sodium and ~11 g sugar per 2 tbsp, with tomato potassium; a tablespoon brushed on is enough.

foods.name: Salsa
foods.kidney_notes: Tomato-based with ~230 mg sodium per 2 tbsp; fresh pico de gallo without salt is the swap.

foods.name: Marinara / spaghetti sauce, jarred
foods.kidney_notes: Tomato sauce is high in potassium (~400 mg per 1/2 cup) and sodium; use 1/4 cup, or a garlic-olive-oil or cream sauce.

foods.name: Hot sauce, sriracha
foods.kidney_notes: ~140 mg sodium per teaspoon; fresh chilli or crushed red pepper is the salt-free heat.

foods.name: Cheese sauce, ready-to-serve
foods.kidney_notes: Jarred cheese sauce is built on sodium phosphate emulsifiers and salt; melt a little real cheddar into rice milk instead.

foods.name: Gravy, beef, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Canned gravy is ~330 mg sodium per 1/4 cup and, being liquid, counts toward a fluid limit; thicken your own pan juices with a little cornstarch.

foods.name: Pickle relish, sweet
foods.kidney_notes: ~120 mg sodium and 4 g sugar per tbsp; a small spoonful is fine.

foods.name: Chicken broth, low sodium, canned
foods.kidney_notes: A good base: ~70 mg sodium per cup versus ~860 mg in regular broth; counts toward fluid.

foods.name: Beef broth / bouillon, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: Bouillon is salt in a cube (~640 mg sodium per cup); low-sodium broth is the swap, and it counts toward fluid.

foods.name: Soup, chicken noodle, canned, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: Canned soup is ~850 mg sodium per cup and counts as fluid; make soup from low-sodium broth, rice and vegetables.

foods.name: Soup, tomato, canned, prepared with water
foods.kidney_notes: Tomato soup is both high-potassium (~680 mg) and high-sodium (~460 mg) per cup; a low-sodium chicken-rice soup is the swap.

foods.name: Soup, cream of mushroom, canned, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: ~870 mg sodium per cup and phosphate stabilisers in many brands; a homemade cream soup with rice milk is the swap.

foods.name: Soup, vegetable beef, canned, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: Canned vegetable soups run ~850 mg sodium per cup; homemade with low-sodium broth is the swap.

foods.name: Soup, vegetarian vegetable, canned, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: ~820 mg sodium and tomato potassium per cup; homemade with leached vegetables is the swap.

foods.name: Clam chowder, New England, canned
foods.kidney_notes: ~870 mg sodium, milk phosphorus and potato potassium per cup; a small bowl occasionally.

foods.name: Soup, lentil with ham, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Lentils plus ham: ~1300 mg sodium and ~350 mg potassium per cup; a low-sodium chicken-rice soup is the swap.

foods.name: Ramen noodles, instant, dry
foods.kidney_notes: A packet is ~1500 mg sodium with phosphate-treated noodles; cook plain noodles or rice with low-sodium broth instead.

foods.name: Chili con carne with beans, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Beans, tomato and salt: ~1000 mg sodium and ~700 mg potassium per cup; homemade chili with fewer beans and no salt is the swap.

foods.name: Macaroni and cheese, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Processed cheese sauce means sodium phosphate and ~740 mg sodium; pasta with a little real cheddar is the swap.

foods.name: Macaroni and cheese, boxed mix, prepared
foods.kidney_notes: The cheese powder is sodium phosphate and salt (~700 mg); cook pasta and melt a slice of Swiss into rice milk instead.

foods.name: Beef stew, canned
foods.kidney_notes: Potatoes, carrots and salt: ~760 mg sodium and ~320 mg potassium per cup; homemade with leached potatoes is the swap.

foods.name: Pizza, cheese, frozen
foods.kidney_notes: Frozen pizza combines processed cheese, phosphate-leavened crust and ~360 mg sodium a slice; one slice on white crust with fresh mozzarella is the compromise.

foods.name: Pizza, pepperoni, frozen
foods.kidney_notes: Pepperoni adds cured-meat sodium to the phosphate-leavened crust and processed cheese; a cheese or vegetable slice is better.

foods.name: Lasagna with meat sauce, frozen
foods.kidney_notes: Tomato, cheese and salt: ~900 mg sodium and ~500 mg potassium per piece; a smaller portion with a side salad.

foods.name: Chicken pot pie, frozen
foods.kidney_notes: A frozen pot pie is ~1300 mg sodium and phosphate-leavened pastry; roast chicken with rice is the swap.

foods.name: Rice bowl with chicken, frozen
foods.kidney_notes: Teriyaki- and sauce-based frozen bowls are ~1200 mg sodium; cook rice and chicken with a splash of reduced-sodium soy.

foods.name: Burrito, bean and cheese, frozen
foods.kidney_notes: Beans, cheese and salt: ~450 mg sodium and ~270 mg potassium; a chicken-and-rice burrito on a corn tortilla is lower.

foods.name: Egg roll, pork, heated
foods.kidney_notes: ~350 mg sodium per roll from soy sauce and the wrapper; one is plenty.

foods.name: Potato salad, home-style
foods.kidney_notes: Potatoes, egg and salt: ~320 mg potassium and ~660 mg sodium per 1/2 cup; use leached potatoes or swap for a pasta or cabbage slaw salad.

foods.name: Coleslaw, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Cabbage is renal-friendly, but fast-food slaw dressing adds ~250 mg sodium and sugar; homemade with vinegar is the swap.

foods.name: Mashed potatoes, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Instant mashed potatoes with gravy: ~350 mg potassium and ~370 mg sodium per 1/2 cup; rice or a roll is the side swap.

foods.name: French fries, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: A medium fries is ~600 mg potassium and ~250 mg sodium; a small, or a side salad, is the compromise.

foods.name: Onion rings, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Battered and salted (~900 mg sodium per order) with phosphate leavening in the coating; a side salad is the swap.

foods.name: Hamburger, fast food, plain
foods.kidney_notes: A plain small burger is the least-bad fast-food choice (~260 mg sodium); skip cheese and ketchup-heavy sauces.

foods.name: Cheeseburger, fast food, with condiments
foods.kidney_notes: Processed cheese adds sodium phosphate and the bun, pickle and sauce push sodium to ~800 mg; order a plain hamburger instead.

foods.name: Chicken nuggets, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Nuggets are brined with sodium phosphate and salted (~570 mg sodium per 6); a grilled chicken piece is the swap.

foods.name: Fried chicken breast, fast food, with skin and breading
foods.kidney_notes: Fast-food fried chicken is phosphate-marinated and salty (~560 mg sodium per 3 oz); remove the skin and breading or choose grilled.

foods.name: Chicken fillet sandwich, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Breaded chicken sandwiches run ~1400 mg sodium with phosphate-brined chicken; a grilled chicken sandwich without pickles is lower.

foods.name: Fish sandwich, fast food, with tartar and cheese
foods.kidney_notes: Breaded fish, processed cheese and tartar sauce: ~580 mg sodium; skip the cheese or choose grilled fish.

foods.name: Taco, beef, hard shell, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Seasoned beef, cheese and the shell: ~275 mg sodium per taco; two is a meal, four is a sodium day.

foods.name: Burrito, bean and cheese, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Beans, cheese and a flour tortilla: ~1000 mg sodium and ~500 mg potassium; a chicken soft taco on corn is the swap.

foods.name: Sub sandwich, turkey/roast beef/ham, 6 in
foods.kidney_notes: Deli meats are phosphate-injected and a 6 in sub is ~720 mg sodium and ~550 mg potassium; roast beef only, no cheese, and ask for less meat.

foods.name: Nachos with cheese, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Nacho cheese sauce is sodium phosphate and salt; plain tortilla chips with salsa is the swap.

foods.name: Biscuit with egg and sausage, fast food
foods.kidney_notes: Phosphate-leavened biscuit plus sausage: ~1100 mg sodium; an egg on a plain English muffin is the swap.

foods.name: English muffin with egg, cheese and Canadian bacon
foods.kidney_notes: Cured bacon and processed cheese add sodium phosphate (~800 mg sodium); ask for egg only on the muffin.

foods.name: Glucose tablet (4 g carb)
foods.kidney_notes: Pure dextrose with no potassium, phosphorus or sodium: the ideal hypo treatment with kidney disease (rule of 15: 4 tablets = 16 g, recheck in 15 min).

foods.name: Glucose gel (15 g carb tube)
foods.kidney_notes: One tube is a full 15 g hypo treatment with no potassium or phosphorus; keep one in every bag.

foods.name: Glucose liquid shot (15 g carb, 2 fl oz)
foods.kidney_notes: A 15 g fast-acting dose with no minerals; the 59 mL counts toward a fluid limit, which is still far less than a glass of juice.
